question.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+3y+z=1 \\ 6x-2y-z=-14 \\ 3x+y-z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $27,$ then $z=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+3y+1z=1 \\ 6x+(-2)y+(-1)z=-14 \\ 3x+1y+(-1)z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}|=27.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{z}$, we replace the third column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 & -14 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -14 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & -14 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-2+14)-3(6+42)+(6+6) \\  & =24-144+12 \\  & =-108.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{-108}{27}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$
